conviction_note: Confirmed the 2026-09-08 bmo print from the company's own 2026-09-01 release; with no option chain and no usable earnings base rate I sized off 183% annualised realised vol (daily sigma ~11.5%) and the one genuine earnings reaction I could identify (Q1 2026, printed 2026-05-19, -13.66%), then netted four primary-filing findings that sum to about -5.5 points, and the dominant setup is a +69.8% 20-day run-up into a quarter whose funded order book (contract liabilities US$7.7m) and encumbered treasury (1,005 of 1,807.6 BTC pledged or locked) are both far weaker than the narrative that drove the run.

findings.finding: The 'digital asset treasury' behind the 2026-08-04 buyback announcement is majority-encumbered: at 2026-03-31 Canaan owned only 802.6 bitcoins outright (plus 63.4 held as customer deposits), while 905.0 bitcoins were pledged for secured term loans and 100.0 more were transferred into a fixed-term product, against US$54.5m of loans (US$21.14m current + US$33.37m long-term).
findings.why_not_priced: The 2026-08-04 release that triggered the re-rating quoted 'approximately US$130 million' of digital asset holdings as of 2026-08-03 with no mention of pledges, and the CEO's quote framed the whole treasury as unrecognised value ('market value does not fully reflect the value of our digital asset holdings'). The stock is +69.8% over 20 days on that framing. If the market had netted off the 1,005 pledged/locked coins it would be comparing a ~US$64m free treasury (at ~US$80k BTC) against a ~US$250m market cap, not a US$130m one, and the asset-backing argument that carried the tape from ~0.21 to 0.3634 would not survive that arithmetic. Corroborating flow arithmetic from a separate document set: Canaan mined 90 + 90 + 64 BTC in Apr/May/Jun and received 3 + 24 BTC from customers, i.e. at least 271 coins in, yet treasury rose only from 1,807.6 to 1,915 (+107) - so roughly 160 coins were liquidated inside Q2 to fund operations, and a further ~44 in July (46 mined, treasury 1,915 to 1,917).
findings.independence: Partly self-contained: the pledge footnote and the loan balances sit in the same 2026-05-19 release, so treat those two as one source. The independent leg is the monthly production filings, which are separate documents and show the net-of-production drawdown: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1780652/000110465926083490/tm2620431d1_ex99-1.htm (2026-07-14, June: 64 mined, treasury 1,915) and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1780652/000110465926097615/tm2623380d1_ex99-1.htm (2026-08-17, July: 46 mined, treasury 1,917).

findings.finding: Canaan's funded forward order book has not been rebuilt: contract liabilities (customer advances) were US$7.739m at 2026-03-31 and US$9.317m at 2025-12-31, against 'nearly $87 million' at 2025-09-30 when over 85% came from North American clients - and no new Avalon purchase-order press release has appeared at any point between June and September 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: The 70% run-up and the hashprice recovery narrative (hashprice +40% off its June low, BTC from US$58.5k at 2026-06-30 to ~US$80k in September) price a demand recovery in the hardware business. Contract liabilities are the only hard, forward-looking, prepaid measure of that demand and they are at 9% of their 2025-09-30 level. Part of the fall is mechanical - the US$87m was drawn down by the 50,000-unit delivery that produced Q4 2025 revenue of US$196.3m - but nothing has replaced it, and Canaan's own historical pattern is to press-release large orders (Cipher, HIVE, the 50,000-unit US order); the last such release I can find is October 2025. If the market had focused on this, the coverage would be arguing about whether Q3 guidance can exceed the US$35-45m Q2 guide at all, rather than treating the Q2 print as a floor. The Jun-30 contract-liability balance in Tuesday's release is the number that settles it, and orders won only after BTC recovered in August would land at 2026-09-30, i.e. not in this filing.
findings.independence: Yes - the US$87m and the 85%-North-America split come from the Q3 2025 earnings call transcript, a different source: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2025/11/18/canaan-can-q3-2025-earnings-call-transcript/ (2025-11-18). The US$9.317m at 2025-12-31 and the Q1-2026 guidance history also appear in the FY2025 release: https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/canaan-inc-reports-unaudited-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-financial-results-302683644.html

findings.finding: Q2 exit-rate was artificially crushed and has already fully recovered: non-JV month-end operating hashrate was 3.36 EH/s against 10.05 EH/s installed at 2026-06-30 (grid maintenance, on top of a 'planned expiration of a hosting agreement' in May that cut non-JV installed capacity from 266.3 MW in April to 246.2 MW), and by 2026-07-31 non-JV operating was back to 10.05 EH/s - equal to installed - with the average revenue split improving from 60.3% to 60.6%.
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody stacks the month-end operating-hashrate rows across four separate 6-K exhibits into a quarter-versus-exit-rate comparison; the aggregators carry only the headline 'BTC mined' line. The consequence is that Q2's mining revenue line will read as a structural collapse (64 BTC in June versus 90 in each of April and May) when the July filing already shows the fleet back at 100% utilisation, which is exactly the mitigant management will lead the 8:00 ET call with. This is the one leg of my set that cuts with the run-up rather than against it, and I have kept it small because the +69.8% tape has plainly absorbed some of the operational recovery already.
findings.independence: Yes - two separate SEC exhibits: the May update giving the 266.3 to 246.2 MW capacity step and the hosting-agreement expiry (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1780652/000110465926072672/tm2617664d1_ex99-1.htm, 2026-06-11) and the July update giving the 10.05/10.05 restoration (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1780652/000110465926097615/tm2623380d1_ex99-1.htm, 2026-08-17). The macro leg is independent too: hashprice recovered 40%+ off its June low per https://nicosmid.substack.com/p/the-hashprice-comeback-how-far-can

findings.finding: Inventory of US$139.1m at 2026-03-31 sits against a Q2 revenue guide of US$35-45m and a Q1 gross LOSS of US$22.9m on US$62.7m of revenue, while the current-generation Avalon A16 (12.8 J/TH, launched October 2025) leaves the A15-era stock as the write-down candidate - Canaan's own self-mining fleet is still running at 23.7 J/TH global and 17.9 J/TH in North America.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus and the wire preview carry a revenue range, not a gross-margin or provision line, and Canaan already hit its Q1 guide (US$60-70m guided, US$62.7m delivered) so revenue is unlikely to be the surprise. The surprise capacity is in the cost line: Q1's negative gross margin means roughly US$42m of inventory left the balance sheet at below cost, and with three-and-a-half quarters of inventory still on hand at a US$40m quarterly run rate, a second provision of similar size is the most likely route to a headline loss well outside anything published. If the market had focused on this, the Q2 discussion would be about the inventory-to-revenue ratio rather than about the BTC treasury.
findings.independence: Weak - the inventory balance and the gross loss both come from the 2026-05-19 Q1 release, which is also the source cluster behind findings 1 and 2; the scorer should collapse those. The genuinely separate leg is the A16 specification and launch date, which establishes the obsolescence gap against Canaan's own 23.7 J/TH fleet: https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/canaan-inc-unveils-next-gen-avalon-a16-series-bitcoin-mining-machine-featuring-breakthrough-asic-chip-302596838.html

searched_and_found_nothing: Nasdaq listing compliance as a fresh catalyst - it is entirely public and stale: initial deficiency notice 2026-01-14, transfer to the Nasdaq Capital Market effective 2026-07-01, second 180-day period applied for 2026-07-06 and running to 2027-01-11 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001780652/000110465926080834/tm2619792d1_ex99-1.htm, 2026-07-06). No reverse-split or ADS-ratio-change document exists on EDGAR; the ADS ratio is still 15 Class A shares per ADS in every 2026 filing I read.

A Citi depositary-receipts 'NOTICE OF ADS RATIO CHANGE / REVERSE SPLIT' PDF (depositaryreceipts.citi.com/adr/common/file.aspx?idf=7873) surfaced in search with a '20% ADS distribution' and June/July 2026 dates, but the PDF would not render to text and I could not read a company name or a date off the document itself - dropped rather than relied on, because it contradicts every SEC filing's 15:1 ratio.

Inter-quarter dilution - no primary source. There has been no 424B5 or new prospectus supplement since 2025-11-04, only a POS AM / POSASR cluster (2026-04-15, 04-28, 05-22, 06-15, 06-16) with an EFFECT order on 2026-06-18, and SEC returned repeated HTTP 503s on those documents. stockanalysis.com shows 744.84m shares versus 690,594,191 ADSs at 2026-03-31, but with no as-of date I will not build a finding on it.

A missing August 2026 production update - the July update was filed 2026-08-17 and the cadence is mid-month (April update 2026-05-14, May 2026-06-11, June 2026-07-14), so nothing is late as of 2026-09-04.

Accounts receivable credit risk, which looked promising and then defused itself: AR went from US$7m at 2025-09-30 to US$51.6m at 2026-03-31 on BTC-collateralised installment sales, but the Q1 release states 'the Company subsequently collected approximately US$42 million in cash from Accounts receivable in April 2026', which removes the provision thesis and is mildly positive for Q2 cash.

Any new Avalon purchase-order or capacity press release between June and September 2026 - none found; the only fresh product news is exhibiting three home miners (Avalon Nano 3S, Mini 3, AvalonQ) at Bitcoin Asia on 2026-08-27/28.

A partner or counterparty disclosure - the JV partner named in the June filing is WindHQ (Alborz facilities, May 2026 wildfire disruption) and it is private, so there is no independent filing to read against Canaan's version.
Careers page, app-store review data and customer support forums - not pursued to any result within budget; I have no evidence either way from these.
baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with, so the only priced statement is the +69.8% 20-day run-up, and three of my four findings cut directly against it - the treasury that justified the re-rating is 56% pledged and the funded order book that would justify a Q3 step-up is at US$7.7m - while the fourth (fleet fully restored by 31 July) is the part the run-up has probably already taken.
